keyFindings.description: NEUTRAL (line 119) admits `!github.event.pull_request.draft` on the grounds that `ready_for_review` builds the head next, but the check never verifies that any pull_request trigger reaching the build lists `ready_for_review`. Reproduced: with `ready_for_review` removed from worker-image.yaml's types at 20fa840c, check-image-trigger-paths.sh exits 0 ('every image trigger covers every input its build reads'), while a draft marked ready without a push would merge with no image build at its final head. The allowlist's own rule is 'unknown means refused, never ungated'. Fix: admit the draft term only when every pull_request/pull_request_target trigger that runs the holder (its workflow, and each caller reaching it through workflow_call) lists ready_for_review in types; add a refused fixture with the default types.

Lines 104 and 108-109: 'a run never cancels a main, workflow_call or workflow_dispatch run' is false for a pending run (GitHub keeps one pending run per group and cancels the older pending one whatever cancel-in-progress says); 'a job group named like its workflow's would wait on itself' is wrong: GitHub detects the deadlock and cancels the run (GitHub docs, concurrency; github/vscode-github-actions#135).

Lines 117-118: a ref key 'would name main's group' is wrong here, since this workflow's non-PR runs key on github.sha; the real reason is the one pr-and-main.yaml gives (the number is the one key that names the pull request on every event).

Lines 6-7 say marking a draft ready starts a run whose checks replace the skipped ones with no condition; GitHub starts no run on a conflicting head, so the skips can stay newest (PR body residual 1). Add the one-line caveat where a future editor reads it.
